title: Brain scoring API v3 — HS curator (hidden-states encoder)
description: brain-api/v2 plus what the HS curator (curator_hs_t3_cand, spec v6828t3) needs: a 27-wide node struct carrying the six re-request columns, an `ext` extension class per node, a 104-col decided row, and per-kind taus in place of the global tau. Text slots are unchanged from v2 (the brain live-encodes the same strings). No cut history crosses the wire: the re-request columns and the fought flag are computed client-side from the freezer's own registry, by chunk identity. score/tools, score/rules and neighbors keep their brain-api/v2 shapes (brain-api-v2.schema.json). The HS brain also accepts brain-api/v2 score/trace bodies through its v2->v3 adapter (docs/brain-api-v3.md). Scores ride the 1e-6 fixed-point grid (engine SCORE_SCALE).

grid_q.description: fixed-point score on the 1e-6 grid (engine SCORE_SCALE): q = round(sigmoid * 1_000_000)

gf.description: doom-head run-state input, CLIENT-computed loop_feats over the conversation's ACTION stream: [current loop fraction, trailing-3 mean, slope over 3 steps, trailing-6 fraction >= 0.34]. Slope can be negative. Omitted = doom not scored.

checkpoint_id.description: sha256 of the checkpoint .pt the client featurized against; the brain 409s on mismatch with its loaded bundle (§8.2 matched-pair trap: features and weights must move together). Retained verbatim from v1 — this guard is the reason v2 is not a promotion of brain-api-dev/v0.

ident.description: bounded identifier charset (conv_id, tool name — harness identifiers)

hex16_id.description: salted 16-hex identity hash. Retained from v1 unchanged: these are the graph's identity/hub keys (equality and truthiness are what ride), and keeping them client-computed keeps graph construction byte-identical to v1. On v2 they are no longer a privacy mechanism — the text they name rides alongside — but they remain the join keys, so do NOT derive them server-side.

text2000.description: chunk/task/system text, CLIENT-truncated to 2000 characters before send. The client truncates (not the server) so the wire stays small and the truncation point is identical to v1's pre-embedding clip — the vectors the server produces must match what v1's client-side embedder would have produced from the same clip.

text240.description: observation head, CLIENT-truncated to 240 characters — the same clip v1 applied before embedding, and the same string head_id salts.

ext_class.description: the chunk file's extension CLASS for the read columns' extension one-hot: one of the 30 extensions the checkpoint knows, 'other' for any other extension, 'none' for no file or no extension (torch_curator.read_columns / _path_v9_ext: lowercase text after the basename's last dot; a leading-dot dotfile has none). A class, not the extension or the name: the file identity stays the salted file_id.

node.description: one live chunk. The v2 node plus `ext`, with a 27-wide struct. The brain computes the 50 read columns from cmd/lo/hi/tokens/kind/step/ext and inserts them after the struct, then appends the role markers and graph-type columns, giving the checkpoint's 106-wide node row. Identical to the v1 node except the three embedding slots carry text instead of vectors; the server embeds them and then rebuilds the exact same graph. EMPTY-STRING SEMANTICS ARE LOAD-BEARING: an empty cmd/head must produce a ZERO VECTOR server-side, not the embedding of the empty string — v1's client mirrored this (featurize::vec_or_zeros never called the embedder on ""), and the parity gate pins it.

text.description: chunk text[:2000] — xe content slot + rel-2 kNN cosine

cmd.description: the producing command, UNTRUNCATED (v1 embedded it untruncated; the clip would change the vector). Empty string when the chunk has none (cmd_id null) -> server emits a zero vector.

head.description: observation head[:240]. Empty string when none (head_id null) -> server emits a zero vector.

struct.description: node_struct_with_type(21) + the six HS re-request columns [n_prior_serves, prior_copy_cut, file_rereq_count, log1p(trace_rereq_count), is_rereq, is_rereq_of_cut], computed client-side over EVERY chunk up to the birth step (dropped ones included) with cut state from the freezer's dropped registry (engine rereq.rs).

tokens.description: chunk token weight (max(1, len(text)//4)); the trace forward reads token mass from `struct`, not from this field

file_id.description: salted hash of the file basename; null = fileless chunk (no rel-0 chain edge, no file hub)

lo.description: first original-file line covered; null disables the rel-0 chain for this chunk

cmd_id.description: salted hash of the producing command string; null = no command (no command hub row)

head_id.description: salted hash of the observation head[:240]; PRESENCE is the has-head marker and gates the head hub on the command's first chunk

score_trace_request.description: POST /v1/score/trace with contract='brain-api/v3' (HS curator). The brain live-encodes nodes[].text/cmd/head, task_text and sys_text with its fine-tuned encoder (Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base final-layer per-token hidden states, 768-token head+tail cap), builds the het graph, fills the read columns and dupcos, and scores the mask rows with the query-bank read head.

target_cov.description: accepted for provenance; tau resolves at bundle load (PARSEC_TARGET_COV), not per request

nodes.description: the LIVE chunk set (client registries applied) in decision order — the stable step-sorted parse order; the temporal chain i->i+1 and all equal-step tie-breaks key on this ordering

task_text.description: the task statement (first user message) text[:2000]; empty string when absent -> zero vector

sys_text.description: system prompt text[:2000] (the harness hub payload); omitted or empty = zeros

mask.description: rows of `nodes` to decide (undecided newborns); all other rows return exactly 1000000 (never cut)

decided_struct.description: one 104-col decided row per mask entry: struct_features 0-15 | rereq 16-21 | read columns 22-71 | age 72 | extra 73-75 | readmit 76-79 | issuematch 80-84 | rerank 85-92 | centrality 93-97 | scout 98-101 | dupcos 102-103. The client fills every block except the read columns and dupcos, which it sends as zeros; the brain fills them. Width is validated against the bundle's read_struct (422 on drift).

edges_supersession.description: client-computed rel-4 pairs [old_src, new_dst] over `nodes` rows (same-file line overlap OR >=0.6 span-set Jaccard). The server sorts pairs lexicographically = the vendored emission order, keeping the scatter summation order bit-identical. Required, even when empty: the client must compute it consciously, never default it away.

scores_q.description: one per node row; rows outside mask are exactly 1000000 (never cut)

doom_q.description: sigmoid(doom head) on the 1e-6 grid — present iff the request carried gf, the checkpoint has a doom head, and a forward ran

embed.description: server-side embed wall time. Unlike v1 (always 0.0) this is a real number on v2 and is the primary capacity signal — it shares the serving lock with the forward (docs/server-side-embedding.md §6).

score_trace_response.description: score/trace reply. Keep rule (client): keep a chunk when it is fought (its struct column 26 = is_rereq_of_cut, known client-side) or scores_q >= tau_q_by_kind[kind]; kinds without a tau (asst) are never cut.

tau_q_by_kind.description: per-kind keep thresholds on the 1e-6 grid, re-derived on the brain's own served scores at the bundle's coverage floor and stored beside the checkpoint. No global tau: one threshold starves the other/reasoning kinds.

bundle_response.description: GET /v1/bundle on an HS brain. The client refuses to score (fail open) unless contracts lists brain-api/v3 and read_struct/node_struct/spec_version equal what it builds.

encoder.description: encoder model name, for ledger provenance
